parsed.explanation: Closest analogue is the 0.65-C profile. A same-sex conduct statute (ss.67, 68, 71) remains on the books, but the dossier records no prosecutions and an overview stating non-enforcement, so it is a tangential secondary signal. The trans-specific impersonation offence was repealed in 2013, and gender presentation is no longer an offence. Social acceptance of trans people is documented through an embedded third-gender tradition, a family-chiefly role, and an overview describing society as very tolerant of being transgender (a single uncorroborated source). A gender-identity aggravator exists at sentencing. Against this, no trans-specific violence rate exists, there is no documented visitor-facing recourse, employment protection covers only sexual orientation, and border, facility and custody practice are unaddressed (open questions, not exposures). The government's rejection of decriminalisation is a modest negative. Net: reduced risk, a step below the acceptance-with-protections tier.
